finding.claim: Hexadecimal/binary/octal number formatting prefixes '0x'/'0b'/'0o' directly to argument.toString(radix). For negative values this yields '0x-A' / '0b-1010' / '0o-12' instead of '-0xA' etc., and for Infinity/NaN/fractions it yields syntactically invalid literals, so the returned JS cannot be evaluated.
finding.title: Negative numbers produce invalid hex/binary/octal literals

verifier.reason: The code at jsesc.js:217-225 directly prefixes '0x'/'0b'/'0o' to argument.toString(radix) with no handling for a leading '-' or for Infinity/NaN/fractional values, so -10 yields '0x-A' and Infinity yields '0xInfinity', both invalid literals, before the plain return at jsesc.js:228-231.

patch.replaceBlock: result = (typeof argument == 'number' && (!Number.isFinite(argument) || !Number.isInteger(argument))) ? String(argument) : hexadecimal.startsWith('-') ? '-0x' + hexadecimal.slice(1) : '0x' + hexadecimal;
patch.rationale: Negative hex values gave '0x-FF' because the sign from toString(16) was after the prefix; moving the sign before the prefix yields '-0xFF', and non-finite/non-integer numbers fall back to decimal String() which is valid JS.
patch.reason: control passed 3/3 and the trigger passed 3/3 after the patch (differential proof)
